high: BATCHING_STATE_CLOSURE: selectTool and apply use functional setters but still read related state from render-scope closures. selectTool reads appliedTool[id], while apply reads selectedTool[id]. Thus the implementation and QA claim that all transition decisions are derived from updater prev is false; a same-batch select→apply sequence can observe stale selectedTool and discard the application.
medium: QA_REGRESSION_VACUOUS: The harness's batching-safety assertion explicitly accepts `!selectedTool[id]` inside the appliedTool updater, so it passes the precise stale render-scope dependency it claims to prevent.

QA_REGRESSION_VACUOUS: The neutral-identity check only requires two occurrences of `📦 異物` across both playing and reflection branches and forbids three exact legacy names. A new fixed identity such as `🥄 金属片` in the playable card could pass while the reflection copy supplies the two neutral-label matches.

IMPLEMENTATION_QA_EVIDENCE_INACCURATE: The claimed card open/close interaction is not implemented: openItem only adds to the Set, the clickable target is the 38px `dx-more` button rather than the full header/card, and applied cards remove the control.

MOBILE_UNIFORMITY_UNSUPPORTED: The implementation QA claims closed and opened cards retain identical heights, but `dx-card` has no fixed/minimum height and opening a card adds variable-length observation text, three tool buttons, and an apply button. The reused responsive classes support width containment but not the claimed height equality.

failure_codes.finding: Functional setters still depend on render-scope sibling state: selectTool consults appliedTool and apply consults selectedTool. This contradicts the required batching-safe prev-derived transition pattern and can lose a same-batch select→apply operation.
The purported batching regression check passes when apply contains the stale closure read `selectedTool[id]`, so its name overstates what it verifies.
The identity regression check counts neutral labels across separate outcome branches and only rejects three exact old names, allowing other fixed material identities in the playable branch.
QA claims card/header open-close behavior and uniform closed/open heights that the JSX and shared CSS do not implement.

recommended_actions: Co-locate each item's opened, selected, and applied fields in one state object and make select/apply transitions depend exclusively on that setter's prev value, following HotelReceiveGame's groupUI pattern.

Rewrite the batching harness assertion to fail on render-scope `selectedTool`/`appliedTool` dependencies inside transition updaters; preferably exercise extracted pure transition functions with sequential same-batch-style inputs.

Scope the neutral-identity assertion separately to the playable and reflection card blocks, require the exact neutral label in each mapped card, and reject any item-specific label/icon source rather than only three historical literals.
Either implement the specified full-card/open-close affordance and uniform card sizing or correct the implementation QA evidence and approved-spec deviation explicitly.
